candidateAudit.text: Charles Barbant | Interrogatoire de Staps par Napoléon He came to kill Napoleon. And he was prepared to try again. In October 1809, while Napoleon was in Vienna, an 18-year-old German named Friedrich Staps tried to approach the French emperor. Staps had come to Vienna with one purpose: to assassinate Napoleon. He considered Napoleon responsible for the wars devastating Europe and decided that he had the right to pass his own death sentence on the emperor. Staps was carrying a knife when he was arrested before he could carry out his plan. Napoleon personally questioned him and reportedly asked what he would do if he were released. Staps’ answer was clear: he would try to kill Napoleon again. Napoleon was struck by the young man’s determination, but the outcome did not change. Staps was found guilty of attempting to assassinate the emperor and sentenced to death. On October 16, 1809, Friedrich Staps was executed by firing squad. He was only 18 years old. The story is sometimes presented as that of a “young idealist” who dared to stand against a powerful emperor. But without the romanticism, the reality is much harsher: a young man deliberately decided to assassinate a political leader and acted on that decision. You may admire or condemn Napoleon and his policies. But that does not turn Staps’ attempted assassination into a heroic act. History is often more complicated than the legends built around it. Where does political protest end — and political murder begin? #history #Napoleon #FriedrichStaps #Vienna #austria

candidateAudit.title: 👑 L'emblématique portrait de l'impératrice par Franz Xaver Winterhalter, le plus intime... Celui où l'impératrice se déleste de la lourdeur de sa couronne pour n'arborer que sa pr
candidateAudit.text: 👑 L'emblématique portrait de l'impératrice par Franz Xaver Winterhalter, le plus intime... Celui où l'impératrice se déleste de la lourdeur de sa couronne pour n'arborer que sa propre légende. Baignée de douceur, Élisabeth s'avance dans la simplicité d'un déshabillé de satin blanc, dont les plis semblent faits de lumière pure. Mais le véritable joyau de cette œuvre est cette cascade souveraine : une chevelure immense, fleuve de soie sombre et de reflets cuivrés, qui s'épanche librement sur son sein. Libérés des exigences de la cour et des épingles impériales, ses cheveux ondulent comme une matière vivante, presque sauvage, qui l'enveloppe et la protège dumonde extérieur. Son regard, empreint d'une douce mélancolie et d'une fierté timide, fixe le spectateur avec une désarmante vérité. C'est le portrait d'une femme rendue à elle-même, captive de sa propre beauté, capturée par le pinceau dans un instant de grâce suspendu, loin du protocole et des faux-semblants de Vienne.

candidateAudit.text: Yesterday, Vienna City Hall became the setting for the 18th Diversity Ball—and what a beautiful celebration it was. People with different backgrounds, identities, experiences and ways of moving, communicating and experiencing music came together to celebrate. I especially appreciated that people with disabilities were present not only among the guests, but also as artists, performers and active participants throughout the evening. Inclusion felt like part of the event’s foundation—not an afterthought. That commitment could be felt in the many accessibility measures: Austrian Sign Language interpretation, accessible facilities, trained assistance, vibration vests through which music could be experienced physically, a Silent Disco and the Dunkelbar hosted by the Austrian Association Supporting the Blind and Visually Impaired. This is what meaningful inclusion looks like: creating a space in which people are considered from the beginning and can participate in ways that work for them. The evening was colourful, joyful and full of energy, but it also carried an important message. Diversity itself is not a barrier. Barriers arise when people and their needs are excluded—and we become stronger when we actively remove them. Thank you, diversityball , for creating a night where diversity was not only celebrated, but genuinely represented and lived. 💗 #diversityball #ViennaEvents #Inclusion #viennaball #wienliebe

Dann kam der Lektor, und mit ihm die Runden, in denen um jeden Punkt und jeden Beistrich gerungen wird. Ein Satz, der beim Schreiben schön geklungen hat, muss am Ende doch weichen, weil er die Abzweigung nicht klar genug erklärt. Im Frühjahr die Fotos: ausgewählt, positioniert, wieder getauscht. Manches Bild hat mehrere Runden gebraucht, bis es dort war, wo es hingehört. Im Sommer war das Buch schließlich druckreif. Und dann kommt der seltsamste Moment am ganzen Vorgang: Man gibt es aus der Hand und wartet. Am Freitag ist das Warten vorbei. ______ Five days to go. After the summer in the saddle came the winter at the desk. Notes, distances, and rather a lot of photographs turned into text. Then came the editor, and with him the rounds where every full stop and comma is fought over. A sentence that sounded lovely while writing has to go in the end, because it doesn't explain the turning clearly enough. In spring, the photographs: chosen, placed, swapped out again. Some needed several rounds before they ended up where they belonged. By summer, the book was ready for print. And then comes the strangest moment of the whole process: you hand it over, and you wait. candidateAudit.text: Next up in our series introducing the artists exhibited at GALIGRÜ: Alma Moos-Nuñez. Alma Moos-Nuñez is a Vienna-based artist. Her work revolves around personal and public memory, traces connections between the internal and existing systems.
